claims.promise: The maker chooses a furniture template and enters finished dimensions, material thickness, kerf, and grain direction; the app derives named parts instead of asking them to start a bare cut-list table.

evidence.finding: The hand-classified woodworking-project-planner result set contained 21/30 woodworking or furniture-design cards while the scan found 16 weak rated incumbents among 22 rated cards.

claims.deferredReason: No template or derivation engine exists; resolve when fixture projects produce the specified named dimensions from finished-size inputs.

claims.promise: The maker can pack derived parts onto their actual sheet and board sizes with kerf, rotation, grain-direction, and offcut constraints, then inspect a labelled cutting diagram and waste estimate.

comparison.limitation: A sampled 2-star review says it did not let the user define sheet size in two dimensions or use scraps.

evidence.finding: CutList Optimizer has 1M+ installs and 9,530 displayed reviews; the sampled weaker Cutting Optimizer review specifically reports missing two-dimensional stock and scrap handling.

claims.deferredReason: No packing solver exists; resolve when deterministic fixtures prove every placed rectangle stays within stock, respects kerf/grain constraints, and reports waste.

claims.promise: For supported mitre, bevel, dado, and frame joints, the maker sees the derived cut angle, mating part, and reference edge alongside the cut diagram rather than a generic angle number.

evidence.finding: The miter-angle screen was mixed with 19 rated cards and 8 weak ratings; the $2.99 Miter Angle listing has 1K+ installs and sampled reviews ask for clearer input and direct-inch entry.

claims.deferredReason: No joint solver exists; resolve when known mitre, bevel, and dado fixtures assert the expected angles and placement distances.

claims.promise: The maker can use the phone's calibrated rotation-vector angle reading as a digital bevel check against the planned angle, without presenting it as a replacement for a precision machinist instrument.

evidence.finding: The digital-angle-finder screen has multiple 1M+ listings and a 50K+ 2.1-star weak incumbent, establishing demand for phone angle measurement but not precision suitability.

claims.deferredReason: No sensor calibration or comparison UI exists; resolve when an instrumentation test maps known simulated rotations to displayed angles and shows the planned tolerance.

claims.promise: The accepted plan leaves the phone as a cut-ready PDF and Android share sheet containing the material estimate, parts, labelled cutting diagrams, and joint settings.

evidence.finding: Across 15 critical reviews in the sampled cut-list pocket, 5 named no value and 2 named missing capability; the quoted woodworking-plan reviews describe single pictures, missing detail, and links that do not work. A complete actionable packet is an inferred functional response to those measured failures.

claims.deferredReason: No PDF or share implementation exists; resolve when an instrumentation test generates the packet and confirms ACTION_SEND with a FileProvider content URI.
